answer: A hash of the work receipt goes up before the task opens, the payload comes down after the slot closes. Receipts expire unless fresh work renews them, so a dormant clone stops counting inside one epoch. Quorum must span unrelated subnetworks, which stops a comet of same-week accounts from co-signing a hollow cluster. The design cannot stop an attacker who pays for real work. It only makes each identity cost one reveal per epoch, and the ripple through the commit log stays visible to anyone reading it.
